disposition_reason: Pilot field study of three organic farms in Ecuador reporting Cd concentration and isotope composition for four whole-bean (with shell) samples and two farm-made cocoa liquors, plus soils, leaves, pod husks, manure and tree litter. No nib/testa separation.

study.material_scope: whole cacao beans with shells; cocoa liquor from Farm A; leaves, pod husks, soils and amendments as context
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Grown in Ecuador: Farm A Sucumbíos (North Amazon), Farms B and C Esmeraldas (Pacific coast); field samples (B and C supplied via the Ethiquable cooperative), not retail
study.sampling_unit: 29 samples total (soils, amendments, plant organs); 4 bean samples (one from mixed C-a/C-b trees) and 2 cocoa liquors; single trees at B, C-a, C-b
study.method: Digestion of 100-200 mg (details in ESI); preliminary Q-ICP-MS; final Cd by 111Cd-113Cd double-spike isotope dilution MC-ICP-MS (Nu Plasma HR)
study.lod_loq: Not reported; procedural blank ~50 pg Cd (<0.1% of sample Cd)
study.basis: dry weight (samples air- then oven-dried at 45 °C; concentrations by isotope dilution MC-ICP-MS)
study.qa: CRMs for soil and plant digestions (ESI Tables S2, S3; 'good agreement'); isotope reproducibility 0.05-0.10 ‰ 2sd

controls.control: Cultivar choice (CCN-51 hybrid vs Nacional hybrid on the same farm)
controls.comparator: Site A-1 Nacional hybrid vs Site A-2 CCN-51 hybrid, Farm A (different soils: Andisol vs Ultisol)
controls.outcome: Bean Cd 1.26 (A-1) vs 2.17 mg/kg (A-2); liquor 1.44 vs 3.95 mg/kg; bean/soil enrichment 3.9 vs 4.1; Δ114/110Cd bean-leaf -0.24 vs -0.08 ‰. Single samples, confounded by soil; isotope differences between cultivars described as tentative.

controls.control: Use of cacao tree litter as organic fertilizer (topsoil Cd enrichment)
controls.comparator: 0-5 cm topsoils vs deeper soils; isotope signatures of litter, manure and soils
controls.outcome: Tree litter 1.15-6.23 mg/kg Cd; two 0-5 cm topsoils (0.515, 1.10 mg/kg) isotopically heavy (~0.2 ‰), attributed to decomposing litter rather than P fertilizer, manure or atmospheric input; chicken manure ~0.27 mg/kg. No bean outcome tested.
Identical leaf-soil and bean-leaf isotope fractionation within error; authors suggest tree age may not substantially affect Cd uptake/translocation. Bean Cd 3.38 (B) vs 3.92 mg/kg (C mixed).

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored bean Cd 'approximately 0.5-2.8 mg/kg ... estimated from figures'; Table 2 gives 1.26, 2.17, 3.38 and 3.92 mg/kg (range 1.26-3.92).
Stored soil Cd 0.3-1.5 mg/kg; Table 2 gives 0.167-1.60 mg/kg.
Stored bean δ114/110Cd 'approximately -0.2 to +0.3 ‰'; Table 2 gives -0.11 to +0.34 ‰.

Stored states lighter isotopes are preferentially retained in beans relative to leaves generally; primary finds this only for Nacional cacao (Δbean-leaf -0.34 to -0.40 ‰), while CCN-51 hybrid shows no resolvable fractionation (-0.08 ± 0.13 ‰).
Stored author list (Maurice, Schreck, Lefeuvre, Uzu, Elustondo, Laux, Luch, Behra, Prunier) differs from primary (Barraza, Moore, Rehkämper, Schreck, Lefeuvre, Kreissig, Coles, Maurice).
Stored matrices/products omit the two cocoa liquor samples (1.44 and 3.95 mg/kg); stored sample_n 3 counts farms, primary analysed 29 samples at five sites.
Stored attributes high Ecuador Cd to 'volcanic parent material plus possible phosphate fertilizer'; primary farms used no mineral P fertilizer and the topsoil enrichment is attributed to tree litter.
Task brief mentions bean/nib/testa values; primary reports whole beans with shells and cocoa liquor only, no nib or testa fractions.
unresolved: Sampling dates are in the ESI (not available locally); years left null.
Fermentation/drying status of the bean samples and how the cocoa liquor was produced are described only in the ESI.
No LOD/LOQ reported in the main text.
